candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers (and whole numbers when needed) into equivalent improper fractions, optionally using a specified denominator to match other fractions.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts define the same operation: rewriting mixed numbers a b/c as (a·c+b)/c and rewriting whole numbers as equivalent fractions to support later common-denominator work.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction over that denominator by scaling numerator and denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe selecting/finding a common denominator and converting each fraction to that denominator (including scaling numerators/denominators).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once they are in compatible forms (e.g., same denominator or separated whole and fractional parts).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts align on the core subtraction step after compatibility is achieved, including subtracting numerators over a shared denominator and/or subtracting whole and fractional parts separately.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms and express it in an acceptable final form such as a simplified fraction, mixed number, or integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include both reduction to lowest terms and final-form formatting (improper-to-mixed and recognizing integer/zero results) as the post-subtraction finishing skill.

alignment_summary: Across the three codebooks, all skills align one-to-one with identical granularity: (1) convert mixed/whole to improper/equivalent fractions, (2) find a common denominator and rewrite equivalent fractions, (3) perform the subtraction in compatible form, and (4) simplify and present the final result. No unique or split skills were present; consensus is 3/3 for all concepts.
